title: Q2 2026: Capacity Hedge Canaries + SLO-driven Autoscale OKRs
creator: Liam O'Connor
description:
Objective: Validate a lightweight, operational pattern that protects customer-facing latency SLOs while reducing reserved-capacity waste through a set of short-lived 'capacity hedge' canaries and SLO-linked autoscale rules. This ticket scopes the Q2 roadmap slice, success metrics, phased milestones, and cross-team dependencies for the Dedicated product line.

Rationale: We frequently see tension between over-provisioning (wasted cost) and under-provisioning (SLO breaches). A repeatable canary + SLO-feedback autoscale loop lets us test hedging strategies in production with reduced blast radius and clear rollback criteria. This work feeds into commercial OKRs around cost-per-token reduction and SLA adherence for Dedicated customers.

Scope:
- Define canary profiles (traffic mix, size, warm pool sizing) for three customer segments (PLG, mid-market, enterprise).
- Implement an automated canary runner that provisions transient pools (hedge lanes) and measures p99/p50 latency, error-rate, and warm-hit fraction over 10-minute windows.
- Integrate SLO signals (latency/error budgets) into autoscale policy engine to trigger controlled warm-ups or fallback to reserved pools.
- Add observability: per-canary dashboards, synthetic prompt sets, and a compact post-run report template.

Non-goals: Full platform-wide prewarm redesign; do not change billing model in this phase. This is an iterative experiment funnel with fast roll-forward/rollback cadence.
success_criteria: 1) Canary harness runs across 3 customer segments with end-to-end automation. 2) Demonstrated reduction in average reserved utilization by at least 8% for pilot groups without >1% increase in p99 latency breaches. 3) Autoscale triggers ingest SLO signals and complete a warm-up within target window in >= 95% of runs. 4) Clear playbook + dashboard for oncall to assess canary health and rollback decisions.
